Project: /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d (Node 22, built-ins only, no npm install). Write node:test tests (node:test + node:assert/strict) for the HTTP routes of server.mjs. Do NOT edit server.mjs, package.json, public/ or .team/. Load skill: tdd-workflow (if unavailable, ignore).

Read first: /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/.team/notes/spec.md (authoritative; "API" section, also Page first bullet), /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/.team/notes/backend-api.md, and the helper /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/test/helpers/server.mjs (use startServer with env {DATA_FILE: <temp>/data.json}, request with exact `target`, postBooking, booking, makeTempDir, JSON_CT). Do not change the helper.

Rules: assert every spec value with exact equality (status, deepEqual of the whole parsed JSON, content-type header === 'application/json; charset=utf-8' exactly). Clean up servers and temp dirs. Functions under 50 lines, file under 500 lines. No console.log. If a test fails because server.mjs breaks the spec, keep it strict and report it precisely.

File: test/api-routes.test.mjs
- GET /api/rooms → 200, deepEqual {rooms:['Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos']}, JSON_CT. With a query '/api/rooms?x=1' same.
- Sorting: create bookings in a scrambled order so that wrong sorts fail: same date+start in Cosmos, Aurora, Borealis created in that order (expect Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos — insertion order and reverse-alphabet would both fail); also add rooms where alphabetical vs room order coincide is fine, but include a case proving sort is by date first (a later date with an earlier start), then start (string HH:MM, e.g. '09:00' before '10:00' and '23:00'), across dates '2026-01-05' vs '2025-12-31'. Compare the entire bookings array with deepEqual, including ids.
  Note: room order Aurora<Borealis<Cosmos happens to be alphabetical too, so also assert that ordering isn't by id or insertion: create Cosmos first (id 1) then Aurora (id 2) at the same date/start and expect [Aurora(id2), Cosmos(id1)].
- Date filter: '?date=2026-11-03' returns only that date (sorted); '?date=2026-11-03&date=2026-11-04' uses the first; '?x=1&date=2026-11-04' works; '?date=2026-11-0%33' (percent-encoded '3') decodes to 2026-11-03 → filtered; '?date=2026%2D11%2D03' same; '?date' → 400 {error:'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'}; '?date=' → 400; '?date=bad', '?date=2026-02-30', '?date=2026-11-3', '?date=+2026-11-03' ('+' decodes to space → 400), '?date=1999-12-31', '?date=2100-01-01' → 400; '?date=2099-12-31' and '?date=2000-01-01' → 200 with [] bookings; '?dates=x' and '?Date=x' → 200 all bookings (param ignored, case-sensitive); '?date=x&date=2026-11-03' → 400 (first wins). Valid date with no bookings → {bookings: []}.
- Byte-for-byte paths: GET of '/api/%62ookings', '/api/./rooms', '/API/rooms', '/api/rooms/', '/api//rooms', '/api/bookings/', '/api/bookings/1/', '/api/bookings//', '//api/rooms', '/index.html', '/app.js/', '/nope' → 404 {error:'not found'}, JSON_CT. Same 404 for POST/DELETE/HEAD... (for HEAD just status 404) on '/api/bookings/' and '/api/bookings/1/' and '/x'. '/api/bookings/' DELETE → 404 'not found' (NOT 'booking not found').
- Methods → 405 {error:'method not allowed'}, JSON_CT: POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/OPTIONS on /api/rooms; PUT/DELETE/PATCH/OPTIONS on /api/bookings; GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/OPTIONS on '/api/bookings/1' and '/api/bookings/abc'; POST/DELETE/OPTIONS on '/' and '/app.js'. HEAD on /api/rooms, /api/bookings, /api/bookings/1, '/', '/app.js' → status 405 (HEAD has no body; check status only).
- DELETE route parsing: create booking id 1; DELETE '/api/bookings/0', '/api/bookings/01', '/api/bookings/abc', '/api/bookings/-1', '/api/bookings/1.0', '/api/bookings/+1', '/api/bookings/%31', '/api/bookings/1%2F', '/api/bookings/1?x' (query: path is /api/bookings/1 → this is the id 1 route → 204 actually; place this case so it is expected 204 and booking gone), '/api/bookings/９' (use encoded? Node's http client rejects non-ASCII in path — use '%EF%BC%99' → 404 booking not found), '/api/bookings/99999999999999999999', '/api/bookings/2' (nonexistent) → 404 {error:'booking not found'} JSON_CT. Then a valid DELETE '/api/bookings/<id>' → status 204, raw body length 0, no content-type header (headers['content-type'] === undefined). Deleting again → 404 'booking not found'. Booking gone from GET.
- Page: GET '/' → 200, content-type exactly 'text/html; charset=utf-8', body equals fs.readFileSync(ROOT/public/index.html) byte for byte (compare Buffers). GET '/app.js' → 200, 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8', equals public/app.js. GET '/?x=1' and '/app.js?v=2' → same. Start the server with cwd = a temp dir (pass cwd option) for these page tests to prove serving does not depend on cwd.
- Content type on all non-page replies with a body: check 200/201/400/404/405/409/413/415 all JSON_CT (a few of these are covered elsewhere; include at least one representative each here via simple requests).
- Error replies have exactly one key: Object.keys(json) deepEqual ['error'].

Run: cd /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d && node --test test/api-routes.test.mjs . Report files, pass/fail counts, and exact expected vs actual for any failure.

content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from user) — owner: supervisor — 2026-11-02 2 3 Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Project's own tests must pass at the end. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. 1	# Backend API notes — owner: backend — 2026-11-02
2	
3	Implements spec.md (Server, API, Booking rules) in `server.mjs` (one ES module, built-ins only).
4	
5	## Scripts (package.json)
6	- `start`: `node server.mjs`
7	- `test`: `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"` — NOT `node --test test/`: on Node 22.23 a folder
8	  argument fails ("Cannot find module"), the quoted glob works. Name test files `test/*.test.mjs`.
9	
10	## Data file layout (strictly validated at startup)
11	```
12	{"nextId": <safe integer >= 1, greater than every id>,
13	 "bookings": [{"id", "room", "title", "date", "start", "end"}, ...]}
14	```
15	- Top level: exactly the two keys `nextId`, `bookings`. Each booking: exactly the six keys;
16	  `id` a positive safe integer, unique; room one of the three; title already trimmed, 1-80;
17	  date/start/end valid by rules 6-8; end > start; no two bookings overlap.
18	- Any failure, or empty/invalid JSON, or a non-ENOENT read error (e.g. a directory) gives
19	  stderr `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>\n` and exit 1. ENOENT (including a
20	  missing parent folder) means `{nextId: 1, bookings: []}`. The file is not created at startup.
21	- Fixture for tests (valid): `{"nextId":5,"bookings":[{"id":2,"room":"Aurora","title":"T","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}]}`
22	- Save: writes `<file>.<pid>.tmp` beside the data file, then renames it over the data file.
23	  Done only on a successful POST (201) or DELETE (204). Memory is updated only after the save
24	  succeeds; on failure the reply is 500 `internal error` and the state (next id too) is unchanged.
25	  Folders are never created (DATA_FILE=`missing/x.json` starts fine, then POST gives 500).
26	
27	## Pages
28	- `GET /` serves `public/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js` serves `public/app.js`
29	  (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`). Read per request from `<folder of server.mjs>/public/`
30	  (via import.meta.url), not cwd. A missing file gives 500 `internal error`. A query is ignored (`/app.js?x` works).
31	  Other methods on these paths give 405.
32	
33	## Behaviour details testing may rely on
34	- stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>\n`. stderr: one line on startup failure
35	  (invalid PORT, bind error, data file), plus one `request failed: ...` line per unexpected
36	  500 (for example a save failure). Expected 4xx replies log nothing.
37	- All requests are queued after their body is fully read, so they are handled one at a time.
38	- The body is always drained; 413 counts every byte received (more than 10000 gives 413), and
39	  only applies after the 415 check (rule order).
40	- Non-page replies: `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`; 204 has no body and no
41	  Content-Type. 405 replies have no Allow header.
42	- Malformed HTTP gets a raw `400 Bad Request` from the clientError handler; aborted
43	  uploads are dropped; the server stays up.
44	- DELETE id: `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and a safe integer, otherwise 404 `booking not found`.
